//: server code and client code both use typescript
server code can be compiled with tsc, but the client code needs to be bundled, so we use esbuild
because esbuild does not type check, we use tsc to type check the client code without emitting code
we use concurrently to run multiple scripts at once
we use npm-watch to copy html and css files when one of them changes
server-html copies HTML views kept on the server (like modals) next to the compiled server code
prod script builds the project and runs the server
dev script runs the server, builds the project, watches for changes, and refreshes the browser
with ENV=development in .env, the server starts browser-sync and nodemon itself (server/services/browserSyncService.ts)
browser-sync and nodemon are dependencies rather than devDependencies because the server imports them
migrations generate to server/services/database/migration/ (must manually input this path)

scripts.build: tsc --project ./server/tsconfig.json && npm run server-html && tsc --project ./src/tsconfig.json --noEmit && esbuild src/main.ts --bundle --outfile=www/main.js && npm run html
scripts.prod: npm run build && npm run start
scripts.dev: tsc --project ./server/tsconfig.json && npm run server-html && concurrently "npm run build:watch" "npm run watch:html" "npm run watch:server-html" "node ./server/comp/main.js"
